findings.summary: With the new ["api", path] args, a real gh error loses its REST path.
findings.evidence: GhCli::gh builds GhFailure.call from `args.get(3)`. That index assumes the `["api","--method",m,path]` shape that api_text builds (gh.rs:674). With the plan's `["api", path]` shape, index 3 is None, so a real 403 or 5xx error would say `gh api failed` and drop the REST path. Fix: Have get_args or GhCli::gh take the call name from the first arg that starts with `repos/` (the tests at gh.rs:1737 already find the path this way). Or have host_rules wrap the error with the branch path so the report or error still names which call failed.

findings.summary: The plan does not handle pagination of the rules/branches list.
findings.evidence: The plan adds no `--paginate` or `per_page` to the args. The rules/branches list is paginated (30 items per page by default, from memory of the GitHub API, not checked here). A branch with more than 30 rules could leave a rule off the first page, and the check would wrongly report it 'not in force'. Fix: Name this limit in the open questions or the module doc. Criterion 3 forbids field arguments, so fixing it would mean changing the criteria. Recording the limit is enough for this job.

findings.summary: Criterion 6 is mostly shown by reading the files.
findings.evidence: The only behavior-like part of the criterion 6 demonstration is that the tests compile in once the module is registered. The doc and CHANGELOG citations can only be read, not run. That is acceptable for a [content] criterion. Fix: Have the evidence quote the exact //! lines and the CHANGELOG lines that cite §3 and §10.

summary: I checked the plan against the snapshot by reading files only; I ran nothing. Everything the plan names exists: the Runner trait with `fn gh(&self, args: &[String])` and GhFailure with status_code in gh.rs; GhClient::api_text, which always adds `--method`, so the reason for bypassing it holds; lib.rs, where `pub mod gh;` comes before `introspect`, so the new line fits in alphabetical order; records-history §3, which states rules (a), (b) and (c); §10 item 1, which asks for the host-rules confirmation; and CHANGELOG [Unreleased] ### Added. The design fits the reading and the criteria. It uses a plain GET with no method override, has three states with Unknown on runner errors or bad JSON, evaluates all three rules on both branches, and states the rulesets-only limit in both the report and the docs. It also covers the earlier findings: the CHANGELOG cites §3 and §10, and the gate evidence cites each command. Each demonstration would fail without its behavior. The work fits one producer run. Two minor issues remain. First, with the new `[\"api\", path]` shape, a real error message would lose the REST path, because GhCli::gh reads it from args[3]. Second, the plan does not handle pagination of the rules list. Neither blocks the plan.
